verses.1:1: The words of Amos, who was among the herdsmen from Tekoa, which he beheld regarding Israel during the days of Uzziah, king of Judah, and during the days of Jeroboam the son of Joash, king of Israel, two years before the earthquake.
verses.1:2: And he said, "The LORD roars from Zion, and utters His voice from Jerusalem; the pastures of the shepherds mourn, and the summit of Carmel dries up."
verses.1:3: Thus says the LORD: "For three transgressions of Damascus, and for four, I will not revoke it, because they threshed Gilead with iron threshing sledges.
verses.1:4: So I will send fire into the house of Hazael, and it shall consume the citadels of Ben-Hadad.
verses.1:5: And I will break the bar of Damascus, and cut off the inhabitant from the Valley of Aven, and him who wields the scepter from Beth-Eden; and the people of Aram shall go into exile to Kir," says the LORD.
verses.1:6: Thus says the LORD: "For three transgressions of Gaza, and for four, I will not revoke it, because they carried away an entire population into exile, to deliver them up to Edom.
verses.1:7: So I will send fire upon the wall of Gaza, and it shall consume her citadels.
verses.1:8: I will cut off the inhabitant from Ashdod, and the one who holds the scepter from Ashkelon; I will turn My hand against Ekron, and the remnant of the Philistines shall perish," says the Lord GOD.
verses.1:9: Thus says the LORD: "For three transgressions of Tyre, and for four, I will not revoke it, because they delivered up an entire exiled community to Edom, and did not remember the covenant of brotherhood.
verses.1:10: So I will send fire upon the wall of Tyre, and it shall consume her citadels."
verses.1:11: Thus says the LORD: "For three transgressions of Edom, and for four, I will not revoke it, because he pursued his brother with the sword and stifled his compassion; his anger tore perpetually, and he kept his wrath forever.
verses.1:12: So I will send fire upon Teman, and it shall consume the citadels of Bozrah."
verses.1:13: Thus says the LORD: "For three transgressions of the sons of Ammon, and for four, I will not revoke it, because they ripped open the pregnant women of Gilead, in order to enlarge their border.
verses.1:14: So I will kindle a fire in the wall of Rabbah, and it shall consume her citadels, amid shouting on the day of battle, with a tempest on the day of the whirlwind.
verses.1:15: And their king shall go into exile, he and his princes together," says the LORD.
verses.2:1: Thus says the LORD: "For three transgressions of Moab, and for four, I will not revoke it, because he burned the bones of the king of Edom to lime.
verses.2:2: So I will send fire upon Moab, and it shall consume the citadels of Kerioth; and Moab shall die amid tumult, with shouting and with the sound of the trumpet.
verses.2:3: And I will cut off the judge from her midst, and all her princes I will slay with him," says the LORD.
verses.2:4: Thus says the LORD: "For three transgressions of Judah, and for four, I will not revoke it, because they have rejected the law of the LORD and have not kept His statutes, and their lies, after which their fathers walked, have led them astray.
verses.2:5: So I will send fire upon Judah, and it shall consume the citadels of Jerusalem."
verses.2:6: Thus says the LORD: "For three transgressions of Israel, and for four, I will not revoke it, because they sell the righteous for silver, and the needy for a pair of sandals—
verses.2:7: those who trample the head of the poor into the dust of the earth, and turn aside the way of the afflicted; a man and his father go in to the same young woman, so as to profane My holy name.
verses.2:8: And they stretch themselves out beside every altar upon garments taken in pledge, and in the house of their god they drink the wine of those who have been fined.
verses.2:9: Yet it was I who destroyed the Amorite before them, whose height was like the height of the cedars, and who was strong as the oaks; yet I destroyed his fruit above and his roots beneath.
verses.2:10: And it was I who brought you up from the land of Egypt, and led you forty years in the wilderness, to possess the land of the Amorite.
verses.2:11: And I raised up some of your sons as prophets, and some of your young men as Nazirites. Is it not indeed so, O sons of Israel?" declares the LORD.
verses.2:12: "But you gave the Nazirites wine to drink, and commanded the prophets, saying, 'You shall not prophesy.'
verses.2:13: Behold, I will press down beneath you, as a cart presses down that is full of sheaves.
verses.2:14: Flight shall perish from the swift, the strong shall not retain his strength, and the mighty man shall not deliver his life;
verses.2:15: the one who handles the bow shall not stand, the swift of foot shall not escape, and the one who rides the horse shall not deliver his life;
verses.2:16: and he who is stout of heart among the mighty shall flee away naked in that day," declares the LORD.
verses.3:1: Hear this word that the LORD has spoken against you, O sons of Israel, against the whole family which I brought up from the land of Egypt, saying:
verses.3:2: "Only you have I known from among all the families of the earth; therefore I will visit upon you all your iniquities."
verses.3:3: Shall two walk together unless they have agreed to meet?
verses.3:4: Does a lion roar in the forest when there is no prey for him? Does a young lion utter his voice from his den unless he has made a capture?
verses.3:5: Does a bird fall into a snare on the earth when no trap is set for it? Does a snare spring up from the ground when it has caught nothing at all?
verses.3:6: If a trumpet is sounded in a city, do the people not tremble? If calamity comes upon a city, has the LORD not done it?
verses.3:7: Indeed, the Lord GOD does nothing unless He has revealed His secret counsel to His servants the prophets.
verses.3:8: A lion has roared—who will not fear? The Lord GOD has spoken—who will not prophesy?
verses.3:9: Proclaim upon the citadels in Ashdod, and upon the citadels in the land of Egypt, and say, "Assemble yourselves upon the mountains of Samaria, and behold the great tumults in her midst and the oppressions within her."
verses.3:10: "They do not know how to do what is right," declares the LORD, "those who store up violence and plunder in their citadels."
verses.3:11: Therefore thus says the Lord GOD: "An adversary shall be all around the land; he shall bring down your strength from you, and your citadels shall be plundered."
verses.3:12: Thus says the LORD: "As the shepherd rescues from the mouth of the lion two legs or a piece of an ear, so shall the sons of Israel be rescued who dwell in Samaria, with the corner of a bed and the damask of a couch."
verses.3:13: "Hear and testify against the house of Jacob," declares the Lord GOD, the God of hosts:
verses.3:14: "For on the day I punish Israel for his transgressions, I will also bring punishment upon the altars of Bethel; and the horns of the altar shall be cut off and fall to the ground.
verses.3:15: I will strike down the winter house along with the summer house; the houses of ivory shall perish, and the great houses shall come to an end," declares the LORD.
verses.4:1: Hear this word, you cows of Bashan, who dwell on the mountain of Samaria, who oppress the poor, who crush the needy, who say to their masters, "Bring, and let us drink!"
verses.4:2: The Lord GOD has sworn by His holiness: "Behold, days are coming upon you when they shall take you away with hooks, and the last of you with fishhooks.
verses.4:3: And you shall go out through the breaches, each woman straight before her, and you shall be cast forth toward Harmon," says the LORD.
verses.4:4: "Come to Bethel and transgress; at Gilgal multiply transgression! Bring your sacrifices every morning, and your tithes every three days.
verses.4:5: Offer a thank offering of leavened bread, and proclaim freewill offerings—make them heard! For so you love to do, O children of Israel," says the Lord GOD.
verses.4:6: "I also gave you cleanness of teeth in all your cities, and lack of bread in all your places; yet you have not returned to Me," says the LORD.
verses.4:7: "I also withheld the rain from you when there were yet three months until the harvest. I made it rain upon one city, and upon another city I did not make it rain; one portion was rained upon, and the portion upon which it did not rain dried up.
verses.4:8: So two or three cities wandered to one city to drink water, and they were not satisfied; yet you have not returned to Me," says the LORD.
verses.4:9: "I struck you with blight and mildew; the abundance of your gardens and your vineyards, your fig trees and your olive trees the devouring locust consumed; yet you have not returned to Me," says the LORD.
verses.4:10: "I sent among you a pestilence after the manner of Egypt; I slew your young men with the sword, along with your captured horses, and I made the stench of your camps ascend even into your nostrils; yet you have not returned to Me," says the LORD.
verses.4:11: "I overthrew some among you, as God overthrew Sodom and Gomorrah, and you were like a firebrand snatched from the burning; yet you have not returned to Me," says the LORD.
verses.4:12: "Therefore thus I will do to you, O Israel; because I will do this to you, prepare to meet your God, O Israel!"
verses.4:13: For behold, He who forms the mountains and creates the wind, who declares to man what his thought is, who turns the dawn into gloom and treads upon the high places of the earth—the LORD God of hosts is His name.
verses.5:1: Hear this word that I lift up over you, a lamentation, O house of Israel:
verses.5:2: "She has fallen; she shall rise no more, the virgin Israel! She lies forsaken upon her land; there is no one to raise her up."
verses.5:3: For thus says the Lord GOD: "The city that marches out a thousand shall have a hundred left, and the one that marches out a hundred shall have ten left, for the house of Israel."
verses.5:4: For thus says the LORD to the house of Israel: "Seek Me and live;
verses.5:5: but do not seek Bethel, and do not go into Gilgal, nor cross over to Beersheba; for Gilgal shall surely go into exile, and Bethel shall become nothing."
verses.5:6: Seek the LORD and live, lest He break forth like fire upon the house of Joseph, and devour it, with no one to quench it for Bethel—
verses.5:7: you who turn justice into wormwood, and cast righteousness down to the earth!
verses.5:8: He who made the Pleiades and Orion, and turns the shadow of death into morning, and darkens day into night; who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out upon the face of the earth—the LORD is His name.
verses.5:9: He flashes sudden destruction upon the strong, so that ruin comes upon the fortress.
verses.5:10: They hate the one who reproves in the gate, and they abhor the one who speaks uprightly.
verses.5:11: Therefore, because you trample upon the poor and exact tributes of grain from him, though you have built houses of hewn stone, you shall not dwell in them; you have planted pleasant vineyards, yet you shall not drink their wine.
verses.5:12: For I know how many are your transgressions and how mighty are your sins—you who afflict the righteous, who take a bribe, and turn aside the needy in the gate.
verses.5:13: Therefore the prudent man shall keep silent at that time, for it is an evil time.
verses.5:14: Seek good and not evil, that you may live; and so the LORD God of hosts shall be with you, just as you have said.
verses.5:15: Hate evil, love good, and establish justice in the gate; perhaps the LORD God of hosts will be gracious to the remnant of Joseph.
verses.5:16: Therefore thus says the LORD God of hosts, the Lord: "In all the broad squares there shall be wailing, and in all the streets they shall say, 'Alas! Alas!' They shall summon the farmer to mourning, and to wailing those skilled in lamentation;
verses.5:17: and in all the vineyards there shall be wailing, for I will pass through your midst," says the LORD.
verses.5:18: Woe to those who long for the day of the LORD! For what purpose is the day of the LORD to you? It is darkness, and not light—
verses.5:19: as if a man fled from a lion, and a bear met him; or went into the house, and leaned his hand against the wall, and a serpent bit him!
verses.5:20: Is not the day of the LORD darkness, and not light—gloom, with no brightness in it?
verses.5:21: "I hate, I despise your feasts, and I will not savor your solemn assemblies.
verses.5:22: Though you offer up to Me burnt offerings and your grain offerings, I will not accept them, nor will I regard the peace offerings of your fattened beasts.
verses.5:23: Take away from Me the noise of your songs; to the melody of your harps I will not listen.
verses.5:24: But let justice roll on like waters, and righteousness like an unfailing stream.
verses.5:25: Did you bring near to Me sacrifices and grain offerings in the wilderness for forty years, O house of Israel?
verses.5:26: So you shall carry away Sikkuth your king and Kiyyun your images, the star of your gods, which you made for yourselves.
verses.5:27: Therefore I will send you into exile beyond Damascus," says the LORD, whose name is the God of hosts.
verses.6:1: Woe to those who are at ease in Zion, and to those who trust in the mountain of Samaria—the notable men of the foremost of the nations, to whom the house of Israel comes!
verses.6:2: Pass over to Calneh and see; and from there go to Hamath the great; then go down to Gath of the Philistines. Are you better than these kingdoms? Or is their territory greater than your territory?
verses.6:3: you who put far off the day of calamity, yet bring near the seat of violence;
verses.6:4: who lie upon beds of ivory and sprawl upon their couches, and eat lambs from the flock and calves from the midst of the stall;
verses.6:5: who chant idly to the sound of the harp, and like David invent for themselves instruments of song;
verses.6:6: who drink from bowls of wine and anoint themselves with the choicest oils, yet are not grieved over the ruin of Joseph!
verses.6:7: Therefore they shall now go into exile at the head of the exiles, and the revelry of those who lounge shall pass away.
verses.6:8: The Lord GOD has sworn by Himself, says the LORD God of hosts: "I abhor the pride of Jacob, and I hate his strongholds; therefore I will deliver up the city and all that fills it."
verses.6:9: And it shall come to pass that if ten men remain in one house, they shall die.
verses.6:10: Then his kinsman, the one who burns him, shall take him up to bring the bones out of the house, and shall say to the one in the innermost recesses of the house, "Is there still anyone with you?" And he shall say, "No." Then he shall say, "Hush! For we must not make mention of the name of the LORD."
verses.6:11: For behold, the LORD commands, and He shall strike the great house into fragments, and the little house into fissures.
verses.6:12: Do horses run upon the rock? Does one plow there with oxen? Yet you have turned justice into poison, and the fruit of righteousness into wormwood—
verses.6:13: you who rejoice in what is nothing, who say, "Have we not by our own strength taken horns for ourselves?"
verses.6:14: "For behold, I am raising up a nation against you, O house of Israel," says the LORD, the God of hosts, "and they shall oppress you from the entrance of Hamath to the Brook of the Arabah."
verses.7:1: Thus the Lord GOD showed me: behold, He was forming locusts at the beginning of the springing up of the late crop; and behold, it was the late crop after the mowings of the king.
verses.7:2: And it came to pass, when they had finished devouring the herbage of the land, that I said, "O Lord GOD, forgive, I pray! How can Jacob stand, for he is small?"
verses.7:3: The LORD relented concerning this. "It shall not be," said the LORD.
verses.7:4: Thus the Lord GOD showed me: behold, the Lord GOD was calling to contend by fire, and it devoured the great deep and was consuming the portion of land.
verses.7:5: Then I said, "O Lord GOD, cease, I pray! How can Jacob stand, for he is small?"
verses.7:6: The LORD relented concerning this. "This also shall not be," said the Lord GOD.
verses.7:7: Thus He showed me: behold, the Lord was standing beside a wall built with a plumb line, and in His hand was a plumb line.
verses.7:8: And the LORD said to me, "What do you see, Amos?" And I said, "A plumb line." Then the Lord said, "Behold, I am setting a plumb line in the midst of My people Israel; I will not pass by them anymore.
verses.7:9: The high places of Isaac shall be made desolate, and the sanctuaries of Israel shall be laid waste; and I will rise against the house of Jeroboam with the sword."
verses.7:10: Then Amaziah the priest of Bethel sent word to Jeroboam king of Israel, saying, "Amos has conspired against you in the midst of the house of Israel; the land is not able to endure all his words.
verses.7:11: For thus Amos has said: 'By the sword Jeroboam shall die, and Israel shall surely go into exile away from its own land.'"
verses.7:12: Then Amaziah said to Amos, "O seer, go, flee away to the land of Judah! Eat bread there, and prophesy there;
verses.7:13: but at Bethel you shall no longer prophesy, for it is the king's sanctuary, and it is a house of the kingdom."
verses.7:14: Then Amos answered and said to Amaziah, "I was no prophet, nor was I a son of a prophet; rather, I was a herdsman and a dresser of sycamore figs.
verses.7:15: And the LORD took me from following the flock, and the LORD said to me, 'Go, prophesy to My people Israel.'
verses.7:16: Now therefore hear the word of the LORD: You say, 'Do not prophesy against Israel, and do not preach against the house of Isaac.'
verses.7:17: Therefore thus says the LORD: 'Your wife shall play the harlot in the city, your sons and your daughters shall fall by the sword, your land shall be divided by a measuring line, you yourself shall die in an unclean land, and Israel shall surely go into exile away from its own land.'"
verses.8:1: Thus the Lord GOD showed me: behold, a basket of summer fruit.
verses.8:2: And He said, "What do you see, Amos?" And I said, "A basket of summer fruit." Then the LORD said to me, "The end has come upon My people Israel; I will not pass by them anymore.
verses.8:3: And the songs of the temple shall turn to wailing in that day," declares the Lord GOD. "Many shall be the dead bodies; in every place they shall cast them out—hush!"
verses.8:4: Hear this, you who trample the needy, and bring the afflicted of the land to an end,
verses.8:5: saying, "When will the New Moon be past, that we may sell grain, and the Sabbath, that we may open the wheat market—making the ephah small and the shekel great, and falsifying deceitful balances,
verses.8:6: that we may buy the poor for silver and the needy for a pair of sandals, and sell even the refuse of the wheat?"
verses.8:7: The LORD has sworn by the pride of Jacob: "Surely I will never forget any of their works."
verses.8:8: Will the land not tremble for this, and everyone mourn who dwells in it? All of it shall rise like the Nile, heave and subside like the River of Egypt.
verses.8:9: "And it shall come to pass in that day," declares the Lord GOD, "that I will make the sun go down at noon, and I will darken the earth in broad daylight.
verses.8:10: I will turn your feasts into mourning, and all your songs into lamentation; I will bring sackcloth upon every waist, and baldness upon every head; I will make it like mourning for an only son, and the end of it like a bitter day."
verses.8:11: "Behold, the days are coming," declares the Lord GOD, "that I will send a famine upon the land, not a famine of bread, nor a thirst for water, but of hearing the words of the LORD."
verses.8:12: They shall wander from sea to sea, and from north even to east; they shall run to and fro to seek the word of the LORD, and shall not find it.
verses.8:13: In that day the fair virgins and the young men shall faint from thirst.
verses.8:14: Those who swear by the guilt of Samaria, and say, "As your god lives, O Dan!" and, "As the way of Beersheba lives!"—they shall fall and shall not rise again.
verses.9:1: I saw the Lord standing beside the altar, and He said: "Strike the capitals, that the thresholds may shake, and shatter them upon the heads of them all. And the last of them I will slay with the sword; not one of them who flees shall get away, and not one of them who escapes shall be delivered.
verses.9:2: Though they dig into Sheol, from there My hand shall take them; and though they ascend to heaven, from there I will bring them down.
verses.9:3: And though they hide themselves at the summit of Carmel, from there I will search them out and take them; and though they conceal themselves from before My eyes at the bottom of the sea, from there I will command the serpent, and it shall bite them.
verses.9:4: And though they go into captivity before their enemies, from there I will command the sword, and it shall kill them; and I will set My eye upon them for evil and not for good."
verses.9:5: The Lord GOD of hosts is He who touches the earth and it melts, and all who dwell in it mourn; all of it rises like the Nile and subsides like the River of Egypt.
verses.9:6: It is He who builds His upper chambers in the heavens, and has founded His vault upon the earth; who calls for the waters of the sea and pours them out upon the face of the earth—the LORD is His name.
verses.9:7: "Are you not like the sons of the Cushites to Me, O children of Israel?" declares the LORD. "Did I not bring up Israel from the land of Egypt, and the Philistines from Caphtor, and Aram from Kir?"
verses.9:8: "Behold, the eyes of the Lord GOD are upon the sinful kingdom, and I will destroy it from the face of the earth—yet I will not utterly destroy the house of Jacob," declares the LORD.
verses.9:9: "For behold, I will command, and I will shake the house of Israel among all the nations, as one shakes in a sieve, yet not a pebble shall fall to the earth.
verses.9:10: All the sinners of My people shall die by the sword, who say, 'The calamity shall not overtake nor confront us.'"
verses.9:11: "In that day I will raise up the tabernacle of David that has fallen, and wall up its breaches; I will raise up its ruins, and rebuild it as in the days of old,
verses.9:12: that they may possess the remnant of Edom, and all the nations that are called by My name," declares the LORD who does this.
verses.9:13: "Behold, the days are coming," declares the LORD, "when the plowman shall overtake the reaper, and the treader of grapes him who sows the seed; the mountains shall drip sweet wine, and all the hills shall flow.
verses.9:14: I will restore the fortunes of My people Israel; they shall rebuild the desolate cities and inhabit them; they shall plant vineyards and drink their wine; they shall also make gardens and eat their fruit.
verses.9:15: I will plant them upon their land, and they shall never again be uprooted from their land which I have given them," says the LORD your God.

notes.1:1: Hebrew noqedim denotes sheepbreeders or livestock raisers, a specialized pastoral occupation also attested in 2 Kings 3:4.
notes.1:3: The graded numerical formula "for three... and for four" conveys an overflowing measure of guilt, and the pronoun "it" refers to the decreed judgment that the LORD will not turn back.
notes.1:15: "Their king" follows the Masoretic vocalization malkam; the same consonants can also be read as Milcom, the national deity of the Ammonites.
notes.2:7: The Hebrew participle rendered "trample" can also mean "pant after," vividly depicting ruthless greed directed against the destitute.
notes.2:8: "The house of their god" translates Hebrew beit eloheihem, distancing the LORD from Israel's compromised sanctuaries where cultic feasting was funded by extortion.
notes.2:13: The Hebrew verb rendered "press down" occurs only in this verse; some interpreters understand it as making the earth groan or creak under a heavy load.
notes.3:3: Hebrew no'adu denotes two parties meeting by prior appointment rather than merely sharing general agreement.
notes.3:11: The opening Hebrew clause is tersely elliptical, literally "An adversary, and all around the land," conveying the suddenness of the impending siege.
notes.3:12: "The damask of a couch" renders the difficult Masoretic phrase uvidmesheq ares, traditionally understood as fine fabric or a small surviving portion of a luxurious couch.
notes.3:15: "The great houses" translates Hebrew battim rabbim, which may also be rendered "many houses."
notes.4:3: Harmon (Hebrew ha-Harmonah) appears only here in the Hebrew Bible and may denote a northern region of exile; the Masoretic verb is vocalized in the active stem though traditionally understood passively.
notes.4:9: Hebrew ha-gazam refers to a devouring species of locust (often called the cutting locust or palmerworm), echoing the covenant curses of Deuteronomy 28.
notes.4:13: The possessive suffix in "his thought" (Hebrew secho) refers to man, declaring that God knows and reveals human thoughts, though some interpret it as God disclosing His own counsel.
notes.5:5: The Hebrew employs sharp wordplay on the northern sanctuaries: Gilgal shall surely go into exile (galoh yigleh), and Bethel ("house of God") shall become nothingness or iniquity (aven).
notes.5:8: Hebrew Kimah and Kesil are ancient astronomical names traditionally identified with the constellations Pleiades and Orion.
notes.5:26: Sikkuth and Kiyyun are Mesopotamian astral deities linked with Saturn, vocalized in the Masoretic text with the vowels of shiqquz ("abomination") to express disdain for idolatry.
notes.6:7: Hebrew marzeach designates a lavish aristocratic banquet or feasting association known for indulgent drinking and revelry.
notes.6:10: Burning a corpse (Hebrew mesarefo) was extraordinary in Israelite custom and signals extreme crisis from plague or siege, while the warning to remain silent reflects terror of drawing further judgment from God.
notes.6:12: The Masoretic text reads babaqarim ("with oxen"), with the rocky ground implied as the field being plowed; some commentators redivide the consonants to read "plow the sea with oxen."
notes.6:13: The Hebrew plays on two Transjordanian towns recently retaken by Israel: "what is nothing" (lo dabar) puns on Lo-debar, and "horns" (qarnayim, a figure for military strength) puns on Karnaim.
notes.7:7: The Hebrew noun anak, occurring only in verses 7-8, is traditionally rendered "plumb line" and may also denote tin or lead used as a sighting weight.
notes.7:9: Here and in verse 16, Isaac is spelled with the consonant sin rather than the usual tsade, an orthographic variant attested in Amos, Jeremiah, and Psalm 105.
notes.7:14: The rare Hebrew phrase boles shiqmim refers to a tender or dresser of sycamore figs who pierced or nicked the fruit to hasten its ripening.
notes.8:2: The vision turns on a Hebrew soundplay between qayits ("summer fruit") in verses 1-2 and qets ("end") in verse 2.
notes.8:4: Ketiv reads anwe ("meek" or "humble"), while the Qere followed here reads aniyye ("afflicted" or "poor" of the land).
notes.8:8: Ketiv reads wnshqh, while the Qere followed here reads wenishqe'ah ("and subside"), matching the parallel imagery in Amos 9:5.
notes.8:14: "The guilt of Samaria" (ashmat Shomeron) condemns the northern cult and may involve a polemical wordplay on a pagan deity name such as Ashimah.
notes.9:6: "Upper chambers" and "vault" depict the heavens and earth as the structured tiers of God's cosmic dwelling.
notes.9:11: The Masoretic Hebrew alternates among feminine plural, masculine singular, and feminine singular suffixes ("their breaches," "his ruins," "rebuild it"), smoothed to "its" and "it" in English.
notes.9:12: Translated strictly from the Masoretic Hebrew ("possess the remnant of Edom"), rather than the Septuagint reading reflected in Acts 15:17.
notes.9:14: "Restore the fortunes" renders the Hebrew idiom shuv shevut, literally "turn the turning" or "bring back the captivity."
